title: 张骞3D历史档案海报
author: Larus Canus
categories: 海报 / 传单,信息图 / 教育视觉,3D 渲染,水墨 / 中国风,角色,文字 / 排版
prompt_en:
Goal: Create a vertical cinematic 3D historical figure archive poster about 张骞, showing an ancient Chinese explorer breaking out of a documentary-style timeline layout with strong depth and motion.

Canvas: Vertical 3:4 poster, sepia desert palette, high-detail realistic 3D render mixed with aged parchment infographic design. Use dramatic backlight, dusty atmosphere, wind-blown fabric, shallow depth of field, and a grand Silk Road expedition mood.

Main subject: A full-body ancient Han dynasty envoy stands in the center foreground on a rocky desert road. His face is intentionally covered by a soft square pixelated blur. He wears layered worn robes, leather belts, travel wraps, boots, and a red-brown scarf blowing in the wind. His left arm stretches forward holding a large unrolled parchment map that projects toward the viewer in forced perspective; the map is labeled in Chinese as 西域线路图 and contains route lines and place names. His right hand holds a tall ceremonial staff with an ornate metal finial and a hanging vertical red banner reading 汉节. Behind him, show a caravan of camels, riders, soldiers, flags, and a distant western-region city gate under a hazy sky with birds.

Left title column: Place huge black ink-brush Chinese calligraphy vertically reading 张骞. Add smaller vertical Chinese descriptors beside it describing him as an opener of the Western Regions and Silk Road pioneer, plus dates “前164—前114” and a small red seal stamp. Keep the typography elegant, historical, and museum-like.

Floating archive panels: Use exactly 6 translucent glass-and-gold-line information cards around the figure, each with thin borders, small glowing corner nodes, miniature monochrome historical scene illustrations, and Chinese headings. Count and place them as follows: 1) upper left card, “01 前138 奉汉出使”, with a small envoy departure scene; 2) upper right card, “02 前129 被匈奴扣留”, with a captivity or horsemen scene; 3) lower left-middle card, “03 前119 再通西域”, with a caravan scene; 4) right-middle card, “04 前115 联络诸国”, with diplomats and allies; 5) lower right card, “05 前114 回到长安”, with return-to-capital imagery; 6) bottom-left large card, “06 丝路初开”, showing a route map and camel caravan.

Bottom timeline: Add one thin horizontal timeline across the bottom with exactly 6 labeled milestones, evenly spaced: “前164 出生 汉中郡城固”, “前138 奉汉出使 出使大月氏”, “前129 被匈奴扣留 持节不屈”, “前119 再通西域 抵达大月氏”, “前115 联络诸国 建立友好”, “前114 回到长安 报告见闻”. Use small serif-like Chinese type, warm off-white ink, and subtle gold tick marks.

Visual style: Epic historical realism, photorealistic cloth and leather textures, parchment infographic overlay, museum exhibition poster, ancient Chinese frontier expedition, desert dust, wind, warm bronze and beige tones, sharp foreground map, cinematic perspective, volumetric light, ultra-detailed 3D立像档案 aesthetic.

Constraints: Preserve exactly one central figure, one large parchment map, one ceremonial staff with one hanging banner, six floating archive cards, and six bottom timeline milestones. Avoid modern objects, avoid extra panels, avoid neon colors, and do not add a watermark.\

Canvas: 1:1 square image, cream lined notebook paper background with rounded corners, blue border line, visible metal spiral binding along the left edge, soft grid-paper tape decoration near the top left, and blue/yellow pen-marker accents. Overall look should be clean, friendly, handwritten, and sketchnote-like.

Text content: Use Japanese handwritten lettering. Top left page marker: “4/4”. Main title inside a blue outlined banner: 実務への接続. Subtitle beneath it: “Manus / Codex / Claude Code / Newsletter”. Mid-page label in a dotted rounded rectangle: “自分のワークフローへ”. Large main message on the lower left: “AIはチャット相手から” above very large bold navy text 作業担当へ. Speech bubble on the right of the character: 毎日の型にする.

Layout: Top third contains exactly 3 connected workflow cards in a horizontal row, each with a numbered blue circle and rounded blue outline. Card 1 is labeled “Manusで収集” and shows a magnifying glass, document, and cloud icon. Card 2 is labeled “Codex/Claude Codeで整理” and shows a clipboard checklist, arrow, folder, and small hierarchy diagram. Card 3 is labeled “ニュースレターで発信” and shows an envelope with a paper and small heart. Add thick blue downward arrows between the cards and another blue arrow down from the center card to the dotted workflow label.

Lower section: On the left, place exactly 3 action rows with circular blue icons and Japanese labels: 1) magnifying glass icon with “調べる”, 2) folder icon with “整える”, 3) envelope icon with “発信する”. Underline or highlight each label with pale yellow marker strokes and dotted guide lines.

She wears a loose blue hoodie and dark skirt, holding a clipboard checklist with exactly 3 checked boxes. Keep the face area intentionally covered by a plain beige rectangular mask, as if anonymized. Use pastel pink hair and blue hoodie if customized.

Visual style: Blue ink line art with occasional navy bold lettering, pale yellow highlights, soft sky-blue scribble fills, small sparkles, hearts, and radiating accent lines. Use a cheerful educational newsletter aesthetic, like a hand-drawn planner page mixed with kawaii anime illustration. Maintain legible text, balanced spacing, and no photorealism.

prompt_en:
Goal: Create a vertical Chinese historical romance character-poster infographic for a noblewoman in an ancient garden, centered on the theme 薛宝钗, with ornate Qing/Hanfu-inspired elegance, scrapbook textures, and numbered story vignettes.

Canvas: Tall 2:3 poster, antique parchment background with torn-paper edges, sepia ink calligraphy, fine gold geometric lines, translucent cracked-glass polygon overlays, and a warm muted palette of beige, cream, dusty rose, sage green, dark ink, and aged gold.

Central subject: Full-body aristocratic young woman standing on a carved round stone pedestal in front of a blurred old library/garden pavilion filled with flowers. Her face is intentionally soft-blurred and featureless, as if anonymized, while the rest of the portrait is highly detailed. She wears an elaborate pale cream embroidered robe with layered wide sleeves, peach-pink translucent outer drapes, sage-green trim, floral peony embroidery down the front panel and hem, embroidered shoes, and a gold-and-pearl hair ornament crown with dangling beads. She holds a round silk fan in her extended left hand, decorated with painted peonies and vertical Chinese calligraphy, and holds a round gold pendant near her chest with the other hand; a tassel and bead chain hang from her wrist. Overall pose: graceful, formal, slightly forward-facing, like a luxury period-drama character reveal.

Main typography: On the far left, place very large vertical black brush-calligraphy reading 薛宝钗. Beneath it, smaller vertical text reads 红楼梦·蘅芜君. Add one small red seal stamp beside the title.

Left-side small labels: Include exactly 3 stacked beige stamp-like tags with dark borders and Chinese text: 1) “端庄温润”, 2) “金玉良缘”, 3) “藏愚守拙”.

Story cards: Arrange exactly 8 numbered vignette cards around the central figure, connected by thin gold lines and triangular geometry. Each card has a dark circular number badge, a Chinese title, a small sepia photo-like inset scene, and two short lines of Chinese explanatory text. The 8 cards are:
1) Top-left card, number 01, title “薛家入京 宝钗初至”, showing a young woman arriving among attendants.
2) Top-right card, number 02, title “蘅芜苑中 香草清芬”, showing a pavilion garden scene.
3) Upper-right card, number 03, title “金锁随身 金玉之说”, showing an indoor seated figure with a blurred face.
4) Mid-right card, number 04, title “冷香丸意 温厚藏心”, showing a young woman writing or studying at a desk.
5) Lower-right card, number 05, title “诗社唱和 才情自敛”, showing a small group gathered around a table with books.
6) Mid-left card, number 06, title “扑蝶花间 春影微动”, showing two young women in a garden.
7) Lower-left card, number 07, title “宝黛钗局 情礼相衡”, showing three people in conversation.
8) Bottom-left card, number 08, title “金玉成婚 梦醒红楼”, showing a wedding or formal gathering scene.

Bottom title plaque: On the pedestal base, add a long gold-edged plaque with the slogan 一柄团扇，半生金玉 in black Chinese calligraphy.

Bottom timeline: Along the very bottom edge, add exactly 5 milestone labels connected by a thin gold line with small circular nodes: “入京”, “蘅芜”, “金锁”, “诗社”, “成婚”.

Visual style: Highly detailed cinematic period-drama poster, antique Chinese manuscript collage, refined feminine luxury, realistic fabric embroidery, botanical peonies, shallow depth of field, soft warm lighting, museum-quality texture, aged paper grain, ink wash details, gold filigree borders, elegant editorial layout.

Constraints: Use Chinese text exactly as specified for all visible titles and labels. Keep the central figure dominant and full-body. Include exactly 8 numbered vignette cards, exactly 3 left-side tags, and exactly 5 bottom timeline milestones. Do not add extra numbered sections, modern objects, logos, watermarks, or English text.\

Main subject: A full-body Ming dynasty admiral in ornate embroidered robes, cloak, belt ornaments, and official headwear stands heroically on the carved wooden bow of a large sailing ship. His right arm thrusts a long rolled nautical map directly toward the viewer, creating strong foreshortening. His left hand rests near the ship rail. Keep the face softly obscured or indistinct, while the costume, posture, and props remain sharp. The figure should feel powerful, statuesque, and breaking out of the poster space.

Background: Massive canvas sails and rigging rise behind him, with faint large Chinese calligraphy on the sail. Sailors and officials occupy the deck to the right. The ship cuts through rough waves, sea spray, and mist. A distant harbor city and fleet silhouettes appear low on the left horizon, with a few birds in the cloudy sky.

Left title area: Large bold black ink-brush Chinese calligraphy reading 郑和. Beside it, add slim vertical Chinese subtitle text: “航海家 · 远洋使节 · 七下西洋”. Add the date range “1371—1433” and a small red seal stamp. Include a narrow vertical note about the Ming dynasty navigator and diplomat opening the maritime Silk Road.

Infographic overlay: Use thin glowing gold lines, corner brackets, small nodes, and translucent parchment-glass rectangles. Include exactly 8 numbered archival cards with small monochrome historical scene images and Chinese captions:

8. “08 1433之后 选择深远” showing ships fading into distance and legacy imagery.

Bottom timeline: Add a thin horizontal gold timeline with exactly 6 labeled milestones: “1371 出生云南”, “1382 入宫服侍”, “1402 受命远航”, “1405 首下西洋”, “1407–1433 七下西洋”, “1433之后 选择深远”. Use small dots and delicate vertical tick marks.

STAGE OPENS — Wide shot showing her isolated on vast dark stage, spotlight above

FREEZE — Sudden sharp freeze pose, one arm extended, other cocked at 90°
GLIDE — Side view of a smooth slide/glide across the floor, low to ground

ATTITUDE — Low angle looking up at her standing dominant, chin down, staring into camera

FINAL SEQUENCE — Multi-exposure ghost effect showing 3 overlapping positions
LAST EIGHT — Teammates/other dancers blur into frame behind her, energy building
THE FINALE — Full extension final pose, arms stretched to ceiling, head thrown back
UNFORGETTABLE — Wide cinematic shot, spotlight beam, smoke/haze, text overlay reads DANCE

prompt_en:
Goal: Create a vintage Chinese food-and-city tourism poster for Wuhan and hot dry noodles, combining local landmarks, regional flavor, and retro print texture.

Canvas: Vertical poster, 4:5 aspect ratio, warm sepia and dark teal palette, weathered halftone paper grain, ink-wash edges, distressed screen-print look, dramatic food photography mixed with illustrated architectural collage.

Layout: Large cream-white Chinese brush calligraphy dominates the upper left reading “武汉 你好”, with the small English subtitle “HELLO WUHAN” below it. The upper right contains a large ornate landmark tower, the Yellow Crane Tower, rendered in golden-brown detail with layered eaves, smoke and mist around its base. Behind it is a faded Wuhan skyline with a long steel bridge crossing the middle left, a riverfront city silhouette, a clock-tower-style historic building on the right, and a thin modern TV tower in the distance. The bottom half is dominated by one large porcelain bowl of noodles in the foreground, cropped close and centered slightly right, steaming and glossy.

Discrete visible elements to include: exactly 1 main food bowl; exactly 1 signature dish inside it, hot dry noodles with thick noodles, sesame paste sheen, chili oil, diced pickled vegetables, sesame seeds, and chopped green onions; exactly 5 major city/landmark background elements: Yellow Crane Tower, Yangtze River bridge, distant skyline, TV tower, and historic clock tower; exactly 1 small red seal stamp near the central title; exactly 1 small red flag on the right-side tower; exactly 3 small foreground garnish/scatter details near the bottom edge: scallion pieces, sesame seeds, and a pair of chopsticks partly visible at the lower right.

Text content: Top left small title “一城一菜” with tiny English “ONE CITY ONE DISH”. Main oversized brush text “武汉 你好”. Red seal text “汉味”. Right vertical Chinese text “热干面” with small vertical English “HOT DRY NOODLES”. Handwritten-style left slogan “芝麻浓香里 藏着武汉清晨”. Bottom left large title “江城面记”, small romanization “JIANGCHENG MIANJI”, and bottom tagline “一城一味 · 一面一故事” with tiny English “ONE CITY, ONE TASTE / ONE BOWL, ONE STORY”. Add decorative blue Chinese writing around the inside rim of the bowl, including “江城面记”.

Visual style: Bold travel-poster composition, retro Chinese advertising poster, high-detail food realism in the foreground, painterly architectural background, rough beige paper texture, navy-blue sky wash, cream calligraphy, deep red accents, burnt orange highlights, cinematic contrast, authentic regional souvenir packaging aesthetic.

Constraints: Keep all visible text legible and placed as described. Do not add extra dishes, people, logos, QR codes, modern UI elements, or watermarks. Maintain a nostalgic cultural food poster feel suitable for restaurant branding, culinary tourism, and city souvenir packaging.\
